9.0.0.en: God appeared to Solomon after he sat on the throne of Israel, at Gibeon, when he offered sacrifices to God (ch. 3) and asked Him to give him wisdom. Now He appears to him a second time, thirteen years after the dedication of the Temple, to declare to Solomon His joy in what he had accomplished and to warn him against being immersed in wealth and the desires of the world, lest he go astray. For he had completed the building of his palaces and had begun to be occupied with the many marriages to foreign women. Here the love of God, His wisdom and His care for His children appear, for He encourages them and warns them against sin before they fall into it.

9.0.1.en: We do not know in what form God's appearance took place, whether a dream or a vision or some other form, such as his hearing a voice or the appearing of a mist or the like, but Solomon was certain that God was speaking to him. Of course he did not see the essence of God, because "No man hath seen God at any time" (Jn 1:18).

9.1.0.en: The Lord told Solomon that his prayer had risen before Him, and here He answers his petitions and declares His good pleasure with what he had done. For when Solomon completed the building of the Temple, his work stopped at that point, but the sanctification of the house is the work of God Himself, declaring His acceptance of this gift. And God, as He declares His presence in the house, reveals what He has decided, namely that from now on He will set His eye, that is, His care, and His heart, that is, His love, upon this house; for God cares for His Temple and for all the acts of worship offered in it. God's care for Solomon's Temple does not mean that it would not be exposed to destruction, as the Jews thought, because He said "for ever," but God keeps His Temple as long as His people are subject to Him and keep His commandments; but when they were occupied away from Him with the worship of idols and evil desires, He refused to dwell among them, and permitted the Temple to be burned by the hand of Babylon (2 Kgs 24), and then by the hand of the Romans. What is meant by His care for His Temple forever is His presence in His Church, which extends forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

9.2.0.en: Here the Lord confirms His promise, conditional upon the continuance of the kingship for the offspring of David, as He had promised his father before, and the condition was perseverance in keeping the commandments with uprightness of heart, as David did.

9.2.1.en: And this is a positive condition, in addition to negative conditions that He will mention in the following verses. The continuation of Solomon's offspring on his throne forever means Christ, who comes from his offspring and reigns forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

9.2.2.en: And God's warning to Solomon to keep His commandments means that he should not be occupied with the love of women and foreign wives, or with the acquiring of gold and the multiplying of horses and various possessions, lest they distract him from God, for the goal of his life is to worship God faithfully.

9.3.0.en: But if the people of God in any generation turn aside from the way of the Lord and His commandments and worship idols, like the nations, then God warns them that He will cast them out of the land that He had given them, and He will neglect the house that He sanctified, so that it will be exposed to ruin, and Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples around them.

9.3.1.en: Despite the clarity of God's words that He could permit His Temple to be destroyed, the Jews continued to believe that the Temple would remain forever, although it was destroyed by the hand of Babylon, and then by the hand of the Romans after the Resurrection of Christ (Lk 19:44). And the Jews still think that they will build the Temple, and they do not want to understand the spiritual meaning, which is faith in Christ and submission to Him, so that He reigns over their hearts in His Church forever.

9.4.0.en: Hiss: a declaration of astonishment and mockery.

9.4.1.en: The Temple, which was a place of pride and honor for the children of Israel, will become an astonishment to everyone who passes by it, who will be amazed at its ruin and ask why the Lord has done so to this land and to this Temple. This was accomplished in 586 BC, when the Temple was destroyed and burned in the Babylonian captivity.

9.5.0.en: The answer to their question will come to them thus: because they forsook the Lord their God, who saved their fathers from Egypt, the house of bondage, and brought them out of it, and they turned aside after other gods, bowed down to them and worshiped them, so all this evil came upon them. And this divine warning is a clear prophecy of the destruction of the Temple.

9.5.1.en: Your way with God, by keeping His commandments, guarantees you rest and joy. So why do you go away from Him, and even provoke Him with your sins and persist in them, and so lose everything? The way of God is always open to you through repentance, so do not neglect it.

9.6.0.en: The building of the Temple took seven years, and the building of Solomon's palace and its annexes took another thirteen years, so the total time those constructions required was twenty years. Solomon built the buildings in this order:

9.6.1.en: 1- The house of the Lord, which is the most important place because it is the place of worship and of meeting with God.

9.6.2.en: 2- Solomon's house, which represents the royal stability and the administration of the kingdom.

9.6.3.en: 3- The house of Pharaoh's daughter, which provides for family stability.

9.6.4.en: 4- The storehouses and the stables for the horses, which arrange the economic needs.

9.6.5.en: We see from the above that Solomon followed the right order in his constructions: the house of the Lord is more important than his own house, and family stability and the administration of the kingdom are more important than the economic matters.

9.6.6.en: May you set the priorities of your life in order, for time is not enough for everything, and therefore your attention to some matters before others, because of their importance, gives you stability. And do not forget, in the press of life, to give priority to your relationship with God and your service.

9.7.0.en: Helped: aided him, that is, helped him quickly.

9.7.1.en: Hiram king of Tyre took care to help Solomon in his many constructions, and Solomon paid him large quantities of wheat, oil and foodstuffs (ch. 5), and Solomon also wanted to complete the rewarding of Hiram for his cooperation with him, but the treasury of the kingdom had run low of money because of Solomon's spending much gold on building palaces and on the many marriages and on acquiring horses, and this is the opposite of what the Law commanded (Deut 17:16, 17). And because of these many costs Solomon was forced to give up 20 cities belonging to the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun, which he had taken, and other cities of the nations, to enlarge his kingdom and fulfill God's promise that the kingdom of Israel would extend from the Euphrates to the river of Egypt; that is, God helped him enlarge his kingdom, but he gave up part of the land that God had given him, and this was of course a mistake on his part, for the Jews held fast to the land and regarded it as a gift from God and an inheritance from the fathers that they could not give up, and so the Law commanded (Lev 25:23). This region, which includes the twenty cities and what is around them, was called Galilee of the Gentiles, because the Gentiles lived in it with the Jews (Isa 9:1, Mt 4:15), and this encouraged idol worship in it, and then idol worship spread through all the land of the people of God, until Christ came and preached in Galilee and drew them to the right faith.

9.8.0.en: Cabul: a mountainous district in Galilee, located southeast of Acre at a distance of ten miles, and its name also means boundary, because it was outside the boundaries of the lands of the children of Israel. Hiram went to inspect those cities, and he did not like them, because their land is mountainous and he prefers cities in the valleys, or on trade routes, or beside the sea, because his main work is trade; so he apologized to Solomon for not accepting these cities, especially since they were friends and brothers and Solomon would not be upset with him.

9.9.0.en: A talent of gold: equals 3000 shekels of gold, and a shekel of gold equals 11-15 g.

9.9.1.en: Hiram sensed the weakness of the financial situation and the scarcity of gold in Solomon's treasuries, so out of the love between them he sent Solomon a gift of 120 talents of gold, and Solomon thanked him, and because of Solomon's faithfulness he considered it a loan that he repaid to Hiram, when he made him a partner in the trade in the ships that Solomon owned, which returned a large financial profit to Hiram (v. 27).

9.10.s.en: (3) Solomon's constructions and his forced labor of the Gentiles

9.10.0.en: Millo: it is the fortress of Zion or the city of David (2 Chr 32:5). Hazor: it was the capital of the kingdom of the Canaanites in northern Palestine (Josh 11); the children of Israel and the Canaanites exchanged control over it, and when Solomon took it he fortified it, and then Tiglath-pileser took it when the kingdom of Assyria attacked Israel (2 Kgs 15:29). Megiddo: it is the one called "Armageddon," that is, the hill of Megiddo, in the Book of Revelation (Rev 16:16). A city of Manasseh located southeast of Haifa by about 32 km, in which there were stables for Solomon's horses.

9.10.1.en: Gezer: an ancient Canaanite city about 30 km west of Jerusalem.

9.10.2.en: Because of the many constructions he undertook, Solomon needed to impose a system of forced labor. The building works he carried out were the Temple and then his palace, and he also renewed the city of David and its walls after they had fallen into ruin with the passing of time, and he built citadels, fortresses and important sites, such as Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer.

9.11.0.en: The children of Israel took Gezer when they entered the land of Canaan, but the Philistines were able to recover it from the children of Israel, and then Gezer began to attack Egypt, so Pharaoh attacked it and took it and burned it and killed those in it, and gave it as a gift to his daughter, as a dowry for her marriage to Solomon, as kings used to do in the past.

9.12.0.en: Nether Beth-horon: a village 20 km north of Jerusalem, built on low ground, and it is one of the cities that David fortified.

9.12.1.en: Baalath: also called "Baalah of Judah" or "Kirjath-baal" or "Kirjath-jearim," where the ark remained for a time, and it is one of the cities of the tribe of Dan (Josh 19:44). It is 15 km west of Jerusalem.

9.12.2.en: Tadmor: it was one of the most beautiful cities of the world, which Solomon fortified to control the routes of the caravans passing through it. It is located 140 miles northeast of Damascus and 120 miles west of the river Euphrates.

9.12.3.en: The wilderness: the desert surrounding the city.

9.12.4.en: The land: the places that Solomon took and that became part of his kingdom.

9.12.5.en: Solomon rebuilt Gezer and also set up many constructions in cities with important locations, namely Nether Beth-horon, and Baalath and Tadmor in the desert lands.

9.13.0.en: That which Solomon desired: that is, the buildings and gardens that he made for his recreation.

9.13.1.en: He also built the cities that had storehouses for agricultural produce and building materials, and the cities that had storehouses for the war chariots and dwellings for the horsemen to live in, for the number of his chariots was large, so he needed several cities in which to put them (ch. 10:26). Thus Solomon made all the structures that he desired, in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all parts of his kingdom, so it was difficult to count all the constructions he made because of their multitude.

9.14.0.en: The Amorites: a people who ruled parts of Palestine and Syria for some time; their line of descent goes back to Canaan, and they remained in the land of Canaan after the Hebrews conquered it.

9.14.1.en: The Hittites: they are the origin of the present-day Armenians and are not Semites. They came to Asia Minor early, and Solomon had Hittite women among his wives.

9.14.2.en: The Perizzites: an important branch of the Canaanite branches who were not wiped out when the children of Israel entered the Promised Land. The Hivites: they are one of the races of the Canaanites.

9.14.3.en: The Jebusites: a Canaanite tribe that lived in "Jebus," which is Jerusalem, and they lived with the children of Judah and Benjamin and continued to hold the fortress of Zion until the days of David, who took their fortress and made it part of Jerusalem, his capital. Some of them remained in the city after David took it, and their presence in the city continued until after the return from the Babylonian captivity.

9.14.4.en: To set up his many structures Solomon needed many laborers, so he used the descendants of the peoples who remained in the Promised Land because the children of Israel were not able to wipe them out: the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of the children of Israel, and Solomon imposed on them forced labor as slaves.

9.15.0.en: Captains: plural of third, which is an advanced military rank: the king is first, the princes are in second place, and then these thirds. They used to ride in the king's own chariot, since each chariot carried three persons.

9.15.1.en: As for the children of Israel, Solomon did not subject any of them to forced labor, but made them soldiers and officers, commanders of chariots and horsemen, and among them were the men of his court and his princes.

9.16.0.en: The number of those who supervised the workers subjected to forced labor for building was 550 men.

9.16.1.en: God blessed Solomon and helped him take many lands to enlarge his kingdom and set up structures for all the needs of the kingdom. God is ready to bless you and everything you do if you submit to His commandments and walk uprightly before Him. So seek God before everything, and He will arrange all your affairs for you.

9.17.0.en: After Pharaoh's daughter moved from the city of David to her palace that Solomon built for her west of the Temple, he built Millo, which is the fortress of Zion, or the city of David, which was mentioned before in (v. 15). And the Book of Chronicles tells us in (2 Chr 8:11) of the reason for which Solomon changed the dwelling of Pharaoh's daughter, for he said, "My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because the places are holy, whereunto the ark of the LORD hath come" (2 Chr 8:11). The ark had earlier come to rest in the city of David (2 Sam 6:12), in the very house of King David, and then Solomon carried it from the city of David, or Zion, to the Temple, so it was not possible for the Gentile wife to dwell in the place that had been sanctified by the presence of the ark of God's covenant.

9.18.0.en: Solomon kept on offering burnt offerings and peace offerings on the bronze altar that he built for the Lord, and he also burned incense on the golden altar by means of the priests three times a year, at the feasts of Passover, Pentecost and Tabernacles, as the Lord's commandment to them. This shows the extent of Solomon's attachment to the worship of God and his personal need of God's blessing in his life.

9.18.1.en: Do not forget, in the press of life, whatever your responsibilities, your need for prayer and for attending church and enjoying the Holy Sacraments, for they are your food and your strength, and by this God dwells in you and you abide in His Church.

9.19.0.en: Ezion-geber: a city at the northern end of the Gulf of Aqaba near the port of Eilat. Solomon built his naval fleet there on the Red Sea, and thereby controlled trade with the Arabian Peninsula, India and the eastern coast of Africa.

9.19.1.en: Eloth: it is the present port of Eilat, and it is located east of Ezion-geber and beside it.

9.19.2.en: The Red Sea: it is the Red Sea.

9.19.3.en: Ophir: a region most likely in present-day Yemen, famous in ancient times for gold. Solomon and Hiram sent their joint fleet to it, which they built from the timber of Lebanon, to bring gold and precious stones.

9.19.4.en: King Solomon cared for trade besides his care for constructions, and he began to build a naval fleet at Ezion-geber, next to the present port of Eilat on the shore of the Red Sea.

9.20.0.en: A strong friendship and a treaty of brotherhood and cooperation bound Solomon to Hiram, so Hiram sent in the ships sailors of great experience in maritime work and the steering of ships, to accompany Solomon's men on their trading voyages and pass on their expertise to them.

9.21.0.en: Among the places to which Solomon sent his ships was the region of Ophir, and he bought from there 420 talents of gold, which is a very large quantity, equal to millions of pounds, and this shows Solomon's wealth. Solomon's wealth and the visit of the queen of Sheba to him
